## ABCB11

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABCB11 encodes bile salt export pump. It catalyzes the transport of the major hydrophobic bile salts, such as taurine and glycine-conjugated cholic acid across the canalicular membrane of hepatocytes in an ATP-dependent manner, therefore participates in hepatic bile acid homeostasis and consequently to lipid homeostasis through regulation of biliary lipid secretion in a bile salts dependent manner. It transports taurine-conjugated bile salts more rapidly than glycine-conjugated bile salts. ([NCBI Gene 8647](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8647), [UniProt O95342](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O95342/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 2 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## ABCC10

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABCC10 encodes ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 10. Based in part on similarity, it is an ATP-dependent transporter of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) family that actively extrudes physiological compounds, and xenobiotics from cells. It does not transport glycocholic acid, taurocholic acid, MTX, folic acid, cAMP, or cGMP. ([NCBI Gene 89845](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/89845), [UniProt Q5T3U5](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5T3U5/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ABCC10 have been reported in glioblastoma, breast carcinoma, and low-grade glioma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ABL1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABL1 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays a role in many key processes linked to cell growth and survival such as cytoskeleton remodeling in response to extracellular stimuli, cell motility and adhesion, receptor endocytosis, autophagy, DNA damage response and apoptosis. Phosphorylation of WASF3 is critical for the stimulation of lamellipodia formation and cell migration. It participates in the regulation of cell adhesion and motility through phosphorylation of key regulators of these processes such as BCAR1, CRK, CRKL, DOK1, EFS or NEDD9. ([NCBI Gene 25](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/25), [UniProt P00519](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00519/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving ABL1 have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia, and b-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## ABL2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABL2 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL2. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays an ABL1-overlapping role in key processes linked to cell growth and survival such as cytoskeleton remodeling in response to extracellular stimuli, cell motility and adhesion and receptor endocytosis. It binds directly F-actin and regulates actin cytoskeletal structure through its F-actin-bundling activity. It participates in the regulation of cell adhesion and motility through phosphorylation of key regulators of these processes such as CRK, CRKL, DOK1 or ARHGAP35. ([NCBI Gene 27](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27), [UniProt P42684](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P42684/entry)). ABL2 can participate in leukemia-associated rearrangements, including fusion with ETV6. ([NCBI Gene 27](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ABRAXAS1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABRAXAS1 encodes BRCA1-A complex subunit Abraxas 1. It participates in DNA damage response and double-strand break (DSB) repair. It forms part of the BRCA1-A complex, acting as a central scaffold protein that assembles the various components of the complex and mediates the recruitment of BRCA1. The BRCA1-A complex specifically recognizes 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitinated histones H2A and H2AX at DNA lesion sites, leading to target the BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer to sites of DNA damage at DSBs. ([NCBI Gene 84142](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/84142), [UniProt Q6UWZ7](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q6UWZ7/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## ACADS

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACADS encodes acyl-CoA dehydrogenase short chain. Based in part on similarity, short-chain specific acyl-CoA dehydrogenase is one of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenases that catalyze the first step of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, an aerobic process breaking down fatty acids into acetyl-CoA and allowing the production of energy from fats. The first step of fatty acid beta-oxidation consists in the removal of one hydrogen from C-2 and C-3 of the straight-chain fatty acyl-CoA thioester, resulting in the formation of trans-2-enoyl-CoA. ([NCBI Gene 35](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/35), [UniProt P16219](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P16219/entry)). Germline disease associations include short chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving ACADS have been reported in glioblastoma, low-grade glioma, and colorectal carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

## ACP6

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACP6 encodes acid phosphatase 6, lysophosphatidic. It hydrolyzes lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) containing a medium length fatty acid chain to the corresponding monoacylglycerol. It has highest activity with lysophosphatidic acid containing myristate (C14:0), monounsaturated oleate (C18:1) or palmitate (C16:0), and lower activity with C18:0 and C6:0 lysophosphatidic acid. ([NCBI Gene 51205](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/51205), [UniProt Q9NPH0](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9NPH0/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ACP6 have been reported in adrenocortical carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and papillary renal cell carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ACSBG2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACSBG2 encodes acyl-CoA synthetase bubblegum family member 2. It catalyzes the conversion of fatty acids such as long chain and very long-chain fatty acids to their active form acyl-CoAs for both synthesis of cellular lipids, and degradation via beta-oxidation. It can activate diverse saturated, monosaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids. It has increased ability to activate oleic and linoleic acid. ([NCBI Gene 81616](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/81616), [UniProt Q5FVE4](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5FVE4/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ACSBG2 have been reported in papillary renal cell carcinoma and clear cell renal cell carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ACTB

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACTB encodes actin, cytoplasmic 1. Based in part on similarity, actin is a highly conserved protein that polymerizes to produce filaments that form cross-linked networks in the cytoplasm of cells. It contributes to the assembly of the gamma-tubulin ring complex (gTuRC), which regulates the minus-end nucleation of alpha-beta tubulin heterodimers that grow into microtubule protafilaments. It forms part of the ACTR1A/ACTB filament around which the dynactin complex is built. ([NCBI Gene 60](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/60), [UniProt P60709](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P60709/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome (autosomal dominant); Baraitser-Winter syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 22366783](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22366783/), [PMID 23649928](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23649928/)). Somatic alterations involving ACTB have been reported in GLI1-altered mesenchymal tumor, malignant/metastasizing. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## ACVR1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACVR1 encodes activin receptor type-1. It participates in negative regulation of signal transduction and positive regulation of DNA-templated transcription. Functional annotations also associate the protein with protein kinase activity and protein serine/threonine kinase activity. ([NCBI Gene 90](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/90), [UniProt Q04771](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q04771/entry)). ## ACVR1B

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ACVR1B encodes activin receptor type-1B. It transduces the activin signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and is thus regulating a many physiological and pathological processes including neuronal differentiation and neuronal survival, hair follicle development and cycling, FSH production by the pituitary gland, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. Activin is also thought to have a paracrine or autocrine role in follicular development in the ovary. Activin binds to type-2 receptor at the plasma membrane and activates its serine-threonine kinase. ([NCBI Gene 91](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/91), [UniProt P36896](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P36896/entry)). Sequence mutations in ACVR1B have been reported in pituitary tumors. ([NCBI Gene 91](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/91)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ADGRA2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ADGRA2 encodes adhesion G protein-coupled receptor A2. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to Wnt7-specific responses, such as endothelial cell sprouting and migration in the forebrain and neural tube, and establishment of the blood-brain barrier. It functions as a Wnt7-specific coactivator of canonical Wnt signaling: required to deliver RECK-bound Wnt7 to frizzled by assembling a higher-order RECK-ADGRA2-Fzd-LRP5-LRP6 complex. It binds to the glycosaminoglycans heparin, heparin sulfate, chondroitin sulfate and dermatan sulfate. ([NCBI Gene 25960](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/25960), [UniProt Q96PE1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q96PE1/entry)).

## ADGRG1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ADGRG1 encodes adhesion G protein-coupled receptor G1. Based in part on similarity, ADGRG1 is coupled to G(12) and/or G(13) G proteins (GNA12 and GNA13, respectively) and mediates the activation Rho small GTPases. It functions as a potent suppressor of ferroptosis: binding to 17-OH-binding initiates signaling that down-regulates CD36 and alleviates ferroptosis-induced liver injury. It mediates cell matrix adhesion in developing neurons and hematopoietic stem cells. ([NCBI Gene 9289](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/9289), [UniProt Q9Y653](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9Y653/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving ADGRG1 have been reported in CNS embryonal tumor with PLAG family gene alteration. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## AFDN

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AFDN encodes afadin. Based in part on similarity, it belongs to an adhesion system, probably together with the E-cadherin-catenin system, which plays a role in the organization of homotypic, interneuronal and heterotypic cell-cell adherens junctions (AJs). May play a key role in the organization of epithelial structures of the embryonic ectoderm. It is essential for the organization of adherens junctions. AFDN is a fusion partner of KMT2A in acute myeloid leukemia, including rearrangements involving chromosomes 6 and 11. ([NCBI Gene 4301](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4301)).

## AGO1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AGO1 encodes protein argonaute-1. It is required for RNA-mediated gene silencing (RNAi). It binds to short RNAs such as microRNAs (miRNAs) or short interfering RNAs (siRNAs), and represses the translation of mRNAs which are complementary to them. It is also required for transcriptional gene silencing (TGS) of promoter regions which are complementary to bound short antigene RNAs (agRNAs). ([NCBI Gene 26523](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/26523), [UniProt Q9UL18](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9UL18/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); neurodevelopmental disorder with language delay and behavioral abnormalities, with or without seizures (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## AGO2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AGO2 encodes protein argonaute-2. Based in part on similarity, it is required for RNA-mediated gene silencing (RNAi) by the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). The 'minimal RISC' appears to include AGO2 bound to a short guide RNA such as a microRNA (miRNA) or short interfering RNA (siRNA). The precise mechanism of gene silencing depends on the degree of complementarity between the miRNA or siRNA and its target. ([NCBI Gene 27161](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27161), [UniProt Q9UKV8](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9UKV8/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Lessel-Kreienkamp syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## AHI1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AHI1 encodes Abelson helper integration site 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in vesicle trafficking and required for ciliogenesis, formation of primary non-motile cilium, and recruitment of RAB8A to the basal body of primary cilium. It forms part of the tectonic-like complex, a complex localized at the transition zone of primary cilia and acting as a barrier that prevents diffusion of transmembrane proteins between the cilia and plasma membranes. ## AHRR

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AHRR encodes aryl hydrocarbon receptor repressor. It mediates dioxin toxicity and is involved in regulation of cell growth and differentiation. It represses the transcription activity of AHR by competing with AHR for heterodimer formation with ARNT and subsequently binding to the xenobiotic response element (XRE) sequence present in the promoter regulatory region of a variety of genes. It represses CYP1A1 by binding the XRE sequence and recruiting ANKRA2, HDAC4 and/or HDAC5. ([NCBI Gene 57491](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/57491), [UniProt A9YTQ3](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A9YTQ3/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## AIP

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AIP encodes the aryl-hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein, rather than the aryl-hydrocarbon receptor itself. It may enhance AHR signaling by influencing ligand responsiveness or movement of the receptor into the nucleus. This interaction places AIP in regulation of receptor signaling without assigning AIP the receptor's own ligand-binding and DNA-binding transcription-factor activities. Pathogenic germline variants are associated with growth hormone secreting pituitary adenoma 1 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

## AKT1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AKT1 encodes RAC-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase. Based in part on similarity, AKT1 is one of 3 closely related serine/threonine-protein kinases (AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3) called the AKT kinase, and which regulate many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis. This is mediated through serine and/or threonine phosphorylation of a range of downstream substrates. AKT is responsible of the regulation of glucose uptake by mediating insulin-induced translocation of the SLC2A4/GLUT4 glucose transporter to the cell surface. ([NCBI Gene 207](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/207), [UniProt P31749](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P31749/entry)). Postzygotic mosaic variants are associated with Proteus syndrome. ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving AKT1 have been reported in juvenile granulosa cell tumor of ovary, malignant adenomyoepithelioma of breast, and papillary carcinoma of breast, invasive. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## AKT2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AKT2 encodes RAC-beta serine/threonine-protein kinase. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine kinase closely related to AKT1 and AKT3. AKT regulates many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis, through the phosphorylation of a range of downstream substrates. ## AKT3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AKT3 encodes RAC-gamma serine/threonine-protein kinase. ## ALK

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ALK encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase with an extracellular region, a single membrane-spanning segment, and an intracellular kinase domain. It has a normal role in nervous-system development and effects on particular neuronal populations. In tumors, ALK can be rearranged, mutated, or amplified. Rearrangements create fusion genes with several different partners, providing a mechanism of oncogenic activation distinct from an isolated kinase-domain sequence substitution. ([NCBI Gene 238](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/238)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with neuroblastoma, susceptibility to, 3 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 18724359](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18724359/)). Somatic alterations involving ALK have been reported in cutaneous melanoma, lung adenocarcinoma, and ALK-positive histiocytosis. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## ALOX12B

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ALOX12B encodes arachidonate 12-lipoxygenase, 12R-type. It catalyzes the regio and stereo-specific incorporation of a single molecule of dioxygen into free and esterified polyunsaturated fatty acids generating lipid hydroperoxides that can be further reduced to the corresponding hydroxy species. Therefore plays a crucial role in the synthesis of corneocytes lipid envelope and the establishment of the skin barrier to water loss. May also play a role in the regulation of the expression of airway mucins. ([NCBI Gene 242](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/242), [UniProt O75342](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O75342/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis 2 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## ALPK1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ALPK1 encodes alpha-protein kinase 1. It may participate in monosodium urate monohydrate (MSU)-induced inflammation by mediating phosphorylation of unconventional myosin MYO9A. APC encodes a tumor suppressor that restrains Wnt signaling and also participates in cell adhesion, migration, and regulation of gene expression. ARID1A encodes a DNA-binding component of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a coactivator of RARA and RXRA through association with NCOA1. It functions as a corepressor for PPARG and suppresses its adipocyte differentiation-inducing activity. It functions as a sensor of N(6)-methyladenine methylation on DNA (6mA): recognizes and binds 6mA DNA, leading to its ubiquitination and degradation by TRIP12, thereby inactivating the PR-DUB complex and regulating Polycomb silencing. Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Bohring-Opitz syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving ASXL1 have been reported in MDS/MPN, NOS, primary myelofibrosis, and systemic mastocytosis. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

([NCBI Gene 55252](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/55252)).

## ATM

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ATM encodes a checkpoint kinase that coordinates responses to DNA damage and helps maintain genome stability. It regulates several downstream proteins by phosphorylation, including p53, BRCA1, CHEK2, RAD17, RAD9, and NBS1. ## ATR

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ATR encodes a serine/threonine kinase that senses DNA stress and activates cell-cycle checkpoints. It phosphorylates proteins that inhibit further DNA replication or entry into mitosis while also supporting repair, recombination, and apoptosis. AURKA encodes aurora kinase A. ## AURKB

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AURKB encodes aurora kinase B. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

AXL encodes tyrosine-protein kinase receptor UFO. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BCL2L12 encodes a BH2-domain-containing regulator of apoptosis. In the cytoplasm it inhibits caspases 3 and 7; in the nucleus it can bind p53 and prevent p53 from associating with target genes. These distinct cellular locations connect inhibition of apoptotic proteases with modulation of a transcriptional stress response. ([NCBI Gene 83596](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/83596), [UniProt Q9HB09](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9HB09/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## BCL6

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BCL6 encodes a transcriptional repressor important for germinal-center B-cell development and regulation of differentiation and DNA-damage-response programs. It forms complexes with different corepressors and histone deacetylases to repress the transcriptional expression of different subsets of target genes. It represses its target genes by binding directly to the DNA sequence 5'-TTCCTAGAA-3' (BCL6-binding site) or indirectly by repressing the transcriptional activity of transcription factors. An important function is to allow GC B-cells to proliferate very rapidly in response to T-cell dependent antigens and tolerate the physiological DNA breaks required for immunoglobulin class switch recombination and somatic hypermutation without inducing a p53/TP53-dependent apoptotic response. ([NCBI Gene 604](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/604), [UniProt P41182](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P41182/entry)). Somatic alterations involving BCL6 have been reported in diffuse large b-cell lymphoma, nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, and DLBCL / high-grade b-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## BCOR

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BCOR encodes BCL-6 corepressor. It participates in negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription and negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. ## BCR

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BCR encodes breakpoint cluster region protein. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein with a unique structure having two opposing regulatory activities toward small GTP-binding proteins. The C-terminus is a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) domain which stimulates GTP hydrolysis by RAC1, RAC2 and CDC42. It accelerates the intrinsic rate of GTP hydrolysis of RAC1 or CDC42, leading to down-regulation of the active GTP-bound form. ([NCBI Gene 613](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/613), [UniProt P11274](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11274/entry)). Somatic alterations involving BCR have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia, and b-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## BIRC3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BIRC3 encodes baculoviral IAP repeat-containing protein 3. It functions as an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase regulating NF-kappa-B signaling. It regulates both canonical and non-canonical NF-kappa-B signaling by acting in opposite directions: acts as a positive regulator of the canonical pathway and suppresses constitutive activation of non-canonical NF-kappa-B signaling. The target proteins for its E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase activity include: RIPK1, RIPK2, RIPK3, RIPK4, CASP3, CASP7, CASP8, IKBKE, TRAF1, and BCL10. ## BRAF

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRAF encodes a serine/threonine kinase in the RAF family that relays growth signals through the MAPK/ERK pathway. This signaling pathway helps regulate cell division, differentiation, and secretion. Activating changes in BRAF can increase this signaling output; V600E is a well-characterized example, but the gene's normal role is to transmit regulated signals rather than maintain continuous pathway activation. ([NCBI Gene 673](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/673)). Germline disease associations include Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GeneReviews: Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1186/), [PMID 16474404](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16474404/)). Somatic activating BRAF mutations occur in melanoma, colorectal and thyroid carcinomas, lung carcinoma, and hairy cell leukemia, among other neoplasms. ([NCBI Gene 673](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/673), [PMID 22817889](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22817889/)).

## BRCA1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRCA1 encodes a nuclear tumor suppressor involved in maintaining genome stability. It works with DNA-damage sensors, other tumor suppressors, and signaling proteins in multiprotein assemblies that coordinate responses to damaged DNA. Its functions include repair of DNA double-strand breaks, recombination, and regulation of transcription. Interactions with RNA polymerase II and chromatin-associated complexes link these DNA-repair functions with regulation of gene activity. ([NCBI Gene 672](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/672)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with BRCA1-related cancer predisposition (autosomal dominant); Fanconi anemia, complementation group S (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 25472942](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25472942/), [PMID 23269703](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23269703/)). Somatic alterations involving BRCA1 have been reported in high-grade serous carcinoma, tubo-ovarian / peritoneal, invasive breast carcinoma, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip), [PMID 24240112](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24240112/), [PMID 21720365](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21720365/), [PMID 25719666](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25719666/)).

## BRCA2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRCA2 encodes a tumor suppressor that maintains genome stability through homologous recombination and protection of DNA replication forks. The protein binds DNA and interacts with RAD51, helping assemble RAD51 filaments at DNA double-strand breaks. It also interacts with PALB2. These coordinated activities support accurate repair during cell division and help protect DNA while it is being copied. ([NCBI Gene 675](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/675)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with BRCA2-related cancer predisposition (autosomal dominant); Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving BRCA2 have been reported in invasive breast carcinoma, high-grade serous carcinoma, tubo-ovarian / peritoneal, and prostate adenocarcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip), [Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [PMID 29610475](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29610475/), [PMID 24240112](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24240112/)).

## BRCC3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRCC3 encodes lys-63-specific deubiquitinase BRCC36. Based in part on similarity, it does not have activity toward 'Lys-48'-linked polyubiquitin chains. It forms part of the BRCA1-A complex, a complex that specifically recognizes 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitinated histones H2A and H2AX at DNA lesions sites, leading to target the BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer to sites of DNA damage at double-strand breaks (DSBs). It is a catalytic subunit of the BRISC complex, a multiprotein complex that specifically cleaves 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitin in various substrates. ([NCBI Gene 79184](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/79184), [UniProt P46736](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P46736/entry)).

## BRD3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRD3 encodes bromodomain-containing protein 3. Based in part on similarity, it is a chromatin reader that recognizes and binds acetylated histones, thereby controlling gene expression and remodeling chromatin structures. It recruits transcription factors and coactivators to target gene sites, and activates RNA polymerase II machinery for transcriptional elongation. It participates in endoderm differentiation via its association with long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) DIGIT: BRD3 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation upon binding to lncRNA DIGIT, promoting binding to histone H3 acetylated at 'Lys-18' (H3K18ac) to induce endoderm gene expression. ([NCBI Gene 8019](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8019), [UniProt Q15059](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q15059/entry)). Somatic alterations involving BRD3 have been reported in NUT carcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## BRD4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BRD4 encodes bromodomain-containing protein 4. Based in part on similarity, it is a chromatin reader protein that recognizes and binds acetylated histones and plays a key role in transmission of epigenetic memory across cell divisions and transcription regulation. It remains associated with acetylated chromatin throughout the entire cell cycle and provides epigenetic memory for postmitotic G1 gene transcription by preserving acetylated chromatin status and maintaining high-order chromatin structure. It also recruits P-TEFb complex to distal enhancers, so called anti-pause enhancers in collaboration with JMJD6. ([NCBI Gene 23476](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/23476), [UniProt O60885](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O60885/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with syndromic intellectual disability (autosomal dominant); Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 29379197](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29379197/)). Somatic alterations involving BRD4 have been reported in NUT carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and prostate adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## BTK

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

BTK encodes Bruton tyrosine kinase, a signaling protein important for B-cell development and transmission of B-cell antigen-receptor signals. ## C6

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

C6 encodes complement C6. It forms part of the membrane attack complex (MAC), a multiprotein complex activated by the complement cascade, which inserts into a target cell membrane and forms a pore, leading to target cell membrane rupture and cell lysis. The MAC is initiated by proteolytic cleavage of C5 into complement C5b in response to the classical, alternative, lectin and GZMK complement pathways. The complement pathways consist in a cascade of proteins that leads to phagocytosis and breakdown of pathogens and signaling that strengthens the adaptive immune system. CAPN1 encodes calpain-1 catalytic subunit. It participates in regulation of catalytic activity and proteolysis. Functional annotations also associate the protein with peptidase activity and calcium-dependent cysteine-type endopeptidase activity. ([NCBI Gene 823](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/823), [UniProt P07384](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P07384/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia type 76 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## CARD11

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CARD11 encodes caspase recruitment domain-containing protein 11. It is an adapter protein that plays a key role in adaptive immune response by transducing the activation of NF-kappa-B downstream of T-cell receptor (TCR) and B-cell receptor (BCR) engagement. It transduces signals downstream TCR or BCR activation via the formation of a multiprotein complex together with BCL10 and MALT1 that induces NF-kappa-B and MAP kinase p38 (MAPK11, MAPK12, MAPK13 and/or MAPK14) pathways. ([NCBI Gene 84433](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/84433), [UniProt Q9BXL7](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9BXL7/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with BENTA disease (autosomal dominant); immunodeficiency 11b with atopic dermatitis (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving CARD11 have been reported in sézary syndrome, diffuse large b-cell lymphoma, and adult t-cell leukemia/lymphoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## CARM1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CARM1 encodes histone-arginine methyltransferase CARM1. Based in part on similarity, it methylates (mono- and asymmetric dimethylation) the guanidino nitrogens of arginyl residues in several proteins involved in DNA packaging, transcription regulation, pre-mRNA splicing, and mRNA stability. It functions as a coactivator for PPARG, promotes adipocyte differentiation and the accumulation of brown fat tissue. It contributes to the regulation of pre-mRNA alternative splicing by methylation of splicing factors. ([NCBI Gene 10498](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/10498), [UniProt Q86X55](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q86X55/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## CASP8

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CASP8 encodes caspase-8. Based in part on similarity, it cleaves and activates effector caspases CASP3, CASP4, CASP6, CASP7, CASP9 and CASP10. The resulting aggregates, named death-inducing signaling complexes (DISCs), perform CASP8 proteolytic activation. Somatic alterations involving CASP8 have been reported in basal cell carcinoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and stomach adenocarcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## CBFA2T3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CBFA2T3 encodes transcriptional corepressor CBFA2T3. Based in part on similarity, it can repress the expression of MMP7 in a ZBTB33-dependent manner. It contributes to inhibition of glycolysis and stimulation of mitochondrial respiration by down-regulating the expression of glycolytic genes including PFKFB3, PFKFB4, PDK1, PFKP, LDHA and HK1 which are direct targets of HIF1A. It regulates the proliferation and the differentiation of erythroid progenitors by repressing the expression of TAL1 target genes. Somatic alterations involving CBFA2T3 have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## CBL

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CBL encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase CBL. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of many signaling pathways by mediating ubiquitination of cell surface receptors. It accepts ubiquitin from specific E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes, and then transfers it to substrates promoting their degradation by the proteasome. It recognizes activated receptor tyrosine kinases, including KIT, FLT1, FGFR1, FGFR2, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, CSF1R, EPHA8 and KDR and mediates their ubiquitination to terminate signaling. ([NCBI Gene 867](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/867), [UniProt P22681](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P22681/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with CBL-related disorder (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving CBL have been reported in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, and acute myeloid leukemia. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## CBLB

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CBLB encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase CBL-B. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase which accepts ubiquitin from specific E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes, and transfers it to substrates, generally promoting their degradation by the proteasome. It negatively regulates TCR (T-cell receptor), BCR (B-cell receptor) and FCER1 (high affinity immunoglobulin epsilon receptor) signal transduction pathways. It also acts by promoting PIK3R1/p85 ubiquitination, which impairs its recruitment to the TCR and subsequent activation. ([NCBI Gene 868](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/868), [UniProt Q13191](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q13191/entry)). Somatic alterations involving CBLB have been reported in lung adenocarcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CCDC6 encodes coiled-coil domain-containing protein 6. ## CDH1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CDH1 encodes E-cadherin, a calcium-dependent protein that mediates adhesion between neighboring cells. The mature protein spans the cell membrane and contains extracellular cadherin repeats and a conserved cytoplasmic tail. Its extracellular region supports cell attachment, while the intracellular region connects adhesion with cellular responses. Loss of E-cadherin function can contribute to tumor progression through changes in proliferation, invasion, and metastatic behavior. ([NCBI Gene 999](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/999), [UniProt P12830](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P12830/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with CDH1-related diffuse gastric and lobular breast cancer syndrome (autosomal dominant); blepharocheilodontic syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving CDH1 have been reported in gastric adenocarcinoma, invasive lobular carcinoma of breast, and stomach adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## CDK6

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CDK6 encodes cyclin-dependent kinase 6. It interacts with D-type G1 cyclins during interphase at G1 to form a pRB/RB1 kinase and controls the entrance into the cell cycle. It is essential for cell proliferation within the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus and the subventricular zone of the lateral ventricles. It promotes the production of newborn neurons, probably by modulating G1 length. ([NCBI Gene 1021](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/1021), [UniProt Q00534](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q00534/entry)). Somatic alterations involving CDK6 have been reported in medulloblastoma. ## CDK8

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CDK8 encodes cyclin-dependent kinase 8. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in regulated gene transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes. Mediator is recruited to promoters by direct interactions with regulatory proteins and serves as a scaffold for the assembly of a functional pre-initiation complex with RNA polymerase II and the general transcription factors. It phosphorylates the CTD (C-terminal domain) of the large subunit of RNA polymerase II (RNAp II), which may inhibit the formation of a transcription initiation complex. ([NCBI Gene 1024](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/1024), [UniProt P49336](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P49336/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with intellectual developmental disorder with hypotonia and behavioral abnormalities (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). CDK8 amplification and increased activity have been described in colorectal cancer, with experimental evidence linking CDK8 to beta-catenin-dependent tumor-cell proliferation. This amplification-associated context is distinct from an isolated sequence variant. ([PMID 18794900](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18794900/)).

## CDKN2A

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CDKN2A produces structurally distinct tumor-suppressor proteins through alternative first exons and reading frames. The p16INK4A product inhibits cyclin-dependent kinase activity, whereas p14ARF stabilizes p53 by interacting with MDM2, a ubiquitin ligase that promotes p53 degradation. ## CTNNB1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

CTNNB1 encodes beta-catenin, a component of adherens junctions that connect neighboring epithelial cells. CYP19A1 encodes aromatase. ## EZH1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

EZH1 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase EZH1. ## EZH2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

EZH2 encodes the catalytic methyltransferase component of polycomb repressive complex 2, which methylates histone H3 lysine 27 to regulate transcriptional repression. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, a Polycomb group (PcG) complex that methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It displays a preference for substrates with less methylation, loses activity when progressively more methyl groups are incorporated into H3K27, H3K27me0 > H3K27me1 > H3K27me2. Somatic alterations involving EZH2 have been reported in follicular lymphoma, primary myelofibrosis, and acute myeloid leukemia. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

GID4 encodes a substrate-recognition component of the CTLH ubiquitin-ligase complex. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

GNAS is a complex imprinted locus with maternally, paternally, and biallelically expressed transcripts. ## H3-3A

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

H3-3A encodes the histone variant H3.3, which is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA replication and contributes to regulation of chromatin structure and transcription. It constitutes the predominant form of histone H3 in non-dividing cells and is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA synthesis. Nucleosomes wrap and compact DNA into chromatin, limiting DNA accessibility to the cellular machineries which require DNA as a template. Histones thereby play a central role in transcription regulation, DNA repair, DNA replication and chromosomal stability. ([NCBI Gene 3020](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/3020), [UniProt P84243](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P84243/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving H3-3A have been reported in malignant giant cell tumor of bone, diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered, and diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3 G34-mutant. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## HDAC1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

HDAC1 encodes histone deacetylase 1. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

HELQ encodes helicase POLQ-like. It is a single-stranded 3'-5' DNA helicase that plays a key role in homology-driven double-strand break (DSB) repair. IL10 encodes interleukin-10. Based in part on similarity, it is a major immune regulatory cytokine that acts on many cells of the immune system where it has profound anti-inflammatory functions, limiting excessive tissue disruption caused by inflammation. Mechanistically, IL10 binds to its heterotetrameric receptor comprising IL10RA and IL10RB leading to JAK1 and STAT2-mediated phosphorylation of STAT3. It targets antigen-presenting cells (APCs) such as macrophages and monocytes and inhibits their release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor /GM-CSF, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor/G-CSF, IL-1 alpha, IL-1 beta, IL-6, IL-8 and TNF. ([NCBI Gene 3586](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/3586), [UniProt P22301](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P22301/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

KAT6B encodes histone acetyltransferase KAT6B. It participates in regulation of DNA-templated transcription and negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription. Functional annotations also associate the protein with transcription coactivator activity and transcription coregulator activity. ([NCBI Gene 23522](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/23522), [UniProt Q8WYB5](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8WYB5/entry)). Germline disease associations include KAT6B-related multiple congenital anomalies syndrome (autosomal dominant); blepharophimosis - intellectual disability syndrome, SBBYS type (autosomal dominant). ## KAT8

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KAT8 encodes lysine acetyltransferase 8. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone acetyltransferase that catalyzes histone H4 acetylation at 'Lys-5'- and 'Lys-8' (H4K5ac and H4K8ac) or 'Lys-16' (H4K16ac), depending on the context. It is the catalytic component of the MSL histone acetyltransferase complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates the majority of histone H4 acetylation at 'Lys-16' (H4K16ac), an epigenetic mark that prevents chromatin compaction. The MSL complex is required for chromosome stability and genome integrity by maintaining homeostatic levels of H4K16ac. ([NCBI Gene 84148](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/84148), [UniProt Q9H7Z6](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9H7Z6/entry)). Germline disease associations include Li-Ghorbani-Weisz-Hubshman syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving KAT8 have been reported in cutaneous melanoma, colorectal carcinoma, and gastric adenocarcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

## KBTBD4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KBTBD4 encodes kelch repeat and BTB domain-containing protein 4. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex which targets CoREST corepressor complex components RCOR1, KDM1A/LSD1 and HDAC2 for proteasomal degradation. RCOR1 is likely to be the primary target while degradation of KDM1A and HDAC2 is likely due to their association with RCOR1. It also targets RCOR3, MIER2 and MIER3 for proteasomal degradation as well as associated proteins ZNF217 and RREB1. ([NCBI Gene 55709](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/55709), [UniProt Q9NVX7](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9NVX7/entry)). Somatic alterations involving KBTBD4 have been reported in medulloblastoma and pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## KCNH5

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KCNH5 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 5. The kinetic is characterized by a slow activation time course and a small voltage dependence of the activation time constants, therefore, starts to open at more negative voltages. The activation kinetics depend on the prepulse potential and external divalent cation concentration. The time course of activation is biphasic with a fast and a slowly activating current component. ([NCBI Gene 27133](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27133), [UniProt Q8NCM2](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8NCM2/entry)). Germline disease associations include neonatal/infantile epilepsy syndrome (autosomal dominant); developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 112 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving KCNH5 have been reported in cutaneous melanoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

## KCNJ12

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KCNJ12 encodes potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 12. It probably participates in establishing action potential waveform and excitability of neuronal and muscle tissues. Inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it. The inward rectification is mainly due to the blockage of outward current by internal magnesium. ([NCBI Gene 3768](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/3768), [UniProt Q14500](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q14500/entry)). Somatic alterations involving KCNJ12 have been reported in breast carcinoma, colorectal carcinoma, and adrenocortical carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## KCNJ8

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KCNJ8 encodes potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 8. Based in part on similarity, inward rectifier potassium channels are characterized by a greater tendency to allow potassium to flow into the cell rather than out of it. KCNQ1 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily KQT member 1. Based in part on similarity, it associates with KCNE beta subunits that modulates current kinetics. ## KCNQ5

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KCNQ5 encodes potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 5. It associates with KCNQ3/Kv7.3 pore-forming subunit to form a potassium channel which contributes to M-type current, a slowly activating and deactivating potassium conductance which plays a critical role in determining the subthreshold electrical excitability of neurons. It also forms a functional channel with KCNQ1/Kv7.1 subunit that may contribute to vasoconstriction and hypertension. ## KDM6A

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

## KIT

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KIT encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase activated by stem cell factor. Its structure includes extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains, a membrane-spanning region, and an intracellular kinase domain. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

KRAS encodes a small GTPase that switches between GDP-bound and GTP-bound states to relay signals controlling cell proliferation and survival. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MALAT1 produces a nuclear long noncoding RNA from a precursor that also yields the small mascRNA product through RNase P cleavage. The mature long RNA lacks a conventional poly(A) tail and is stabilized by a triple-helical structure at its 3' end. It is thought to act as a scaffold for ribonucleoprotein assemblies and participates in regulation of gene expression and the cell cycle. ([NCBI Gene 378938](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/378938)). Somatic alterations involving MALAT1 have been reported in gastroblastoma, TFEB-altered renal cell carcinoma, and GLI1-altered mesenchymal tumor, malignant/metastasizing. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## MALT1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MALT1 encodes mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it mediates BCL10 cleavage: MALT1-dependent BCL10 cleavage plays an important role in T-cell antigen receptor-induced integrin adhesion. It participates in the induction of T helper 17 cells (Th17) differentiation. It cleaves RC3H1 and ZC3H12A in response to T-cell receptor (TCR) stimulation which releases their cooperatively repressed targets to promote Th17 cell differentiation. Pathogenic germline variants are associated with combined immunodeficiency due to MALT1 deficiency (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 23727036](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23727036/)). Somatic alterations involving MALT1 have been reported in marginal zone lymphoma and diffuse large b-Cell lymphoma, NOS. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## MAP2K4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MAP2K4 encodes dual specificity mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 4. It is an essential component of the stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinase (SAP/JNK) signaling pathway. With MAP2K7/MKK7, is the one of the only known kinase to directly activate the stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinases MAPK8/JNK1, MAPK9/JNK2 and MAPK10/JNK3. The phosphorylation of the Thr residue by MAP2K7/MKK7 seems to be the prerequisite for JNK activation at least in response to pro-inflammatory cytokines, while other stimuli activate both MAP2K4/MKK4 and MAP2K7/MKK7 which synergistically phosphorylate JNKs. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MAP3K8 encodes mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 8. MEF2C encodes myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2C. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription activator which binds specifically to the MEF2 element present in the regulatory regions of many muscle-specific genes. It controls cardiac morphogenesis and myogenesis, and is also involved in vascular development. It enhances transcriptional activation mediated by SOX18. ([NCBI Gene 4208](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4208), [UniProt Q06413](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q06413/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, stereotypic hand movements, and impaired language (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving MEF2C have been reported in microsecretory adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## MEF2D

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MEF2D encodes myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D. Based in part on similarity, it mediates cellular functions not only in skeletal and cardiac muscle development, but also in neuronal differentiation and survival. It plays diverse roles in the control of cell growth, survival and apoptosis via p38 MAPK signaling in muscle-specific and/or growth factor-related transcription. It contributes to the regulation of neuronal apoptosis. ([NCBI Gene 4209](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4209), [UniProt Q14814](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q14814/entry)). Somatic alterations involving MEF2D have been reported in b-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## MEN1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MEN1 encodes menin, a tumor-suppressor scaffold protein involved in histone modification and epigenetic regulation of gene expression. Menin helps organize protein interactions that alter chromatin structure and thereby influence transcription. Its scaffold role connects chromatin-associated regulatory proteins rather than specifying a single enzymatic reaction. Changes in these protein assemblies can affect multiple pathways through altered regulation of gene activity. ([NCBI Gene 4221](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4221), [UniProt O00255](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O00255/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 28969599](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28969599/)). Somatic alterations involving MEN1 have been reported in adrenocortical carcinoma, pulmonary carcinoid tumor, and thymic neuroendocrine tumor. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## MET

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MET encodes the receptor tyrosine kinase for hepatocyte growth factor. The precursor protein is processed into alpha and beta subunits linked by disulfide bonds. Ligand binding promotes receptor dimerization and activation, supporting survival, embryonic development, migration, and invasion. MET signaling therefore connects an extracellular growth factor with several cellular responses; increased receptor abundance and sequence alterations represent different ways in which this signaling system can be disrupted. ([NCBI Gene 4233](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4233)). Germline disease associations include papillary renal cell carcinoma (autosomal dominant); hereditary papillary renal cell carcinoma (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving MET have been reported in lung adenocarcinoma, gastric adenocarcinoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## METTL14

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

METTL14 encodes methyltransferase 14, N6-adenosine-methyltransferase non-catalytic subunit. Based in part on similarity, the METTL3-METTL14 heterodimer forms a N6-methyltransferase complex that methylates adenosine residues at the N(6) position of some mRNAs and regulates the circadian clock, differentiation of embryonic stem cells and cortical neurogenesis. M6A regulates spermatogonial differentiation and meiosis and is essential for male fertility and spermatogenesis. M6A also regulates cortical neurogenesis: m6A methylation of transcripts related to transcription factors, neural stem cells, the cell cycle and neuronal differentiation during brain development promotes their destabilization and decay, promoting differentiation of radial glial cells. Somatic alterations involving METTL14 have been reported in endometrial carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and pancreatic adenocarcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## MGAM

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MGAM encodes maltase-glucoamylase. It cleaves the non-reducing alpha-(1,4)-linked glucose residue in linear dextrins with retention of anomeric center stereochemistry. ## MGMT

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MGMT encodes methylated-DNA--protein-cysteine methyltransferase. It participates in the cellular defense against the biological effects of O6-methylguanine (O6-MeG) and O4-methylthymine (O4-MeT) in DNA. It repairs the methylated nucleobase in DNA by stoichiometrically transferring the methyl group to a cysteine residue in the enzyme. This is a suicide reaction: the enzyme is irreversibly inactivated. ([NCBI Gene 4255](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4255), [UniProt P16455](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P16455/entry)). MGMT promoter methylation is a tumor-associated epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing studied in glioblastoma. ([PMID 15758010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15758010/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## MIR143

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MIR143 encodes a microRNA precursor rather than a protein. MicroRNA production involves sequential processing of a primary transcript by DROSHA and DICER, followed by incorporation of the mature small RNA into a silencing complex. Base pairing with target messenger RNAs can reduce their translation or stability. The RefSeq record represents the precursor stem-loop, distinguishing the genomic precursor from the mature regulatory RNA. ([NCBI Gene 406935](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/406935)). Somatic alterations involving MIR143 have been reported in glomus tumor, malignant. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## MIR17HG

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MIR17HG is a noncoding host gene for the MIR17-92 cluster, which contains at least six microRNAs. These regulatory RNAs have roles in survival, proliferation, differentiation, and angiogenesis. Not all host-gene transcripts contain the complete cluster: the longer polycistronic transcript carries it, whereas another noncoding transcript does not. Transcript structure is therefore relevant to the gene's normal regulatory output. ([NCBI Gene 407975](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/407975), [UniProt Q75NE6](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q75NE6/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Feingold syndrome type 2 (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 21892160](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21892160/)). Somatic alterations involving MIR17HG have been reported in embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## MITF

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MITF encodes microphthalmia-associated transcription factor. It is a transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of melanocyte survival and differentiation as well as melanosome biogenesis. It binds to M-boxes (5'-TCATGTG-3') and symmetrical DNA sequences (E-boxes) (5'-CACGTG-3') found in the promoter of pigmentation genes, such as tyrosinase (TYR). It participates in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, MITF phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its inactivation. Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Waardenburg syndrome type 2 (autosomal dominant); Waardenburg syndrome type 2A (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## MKI67

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MKI67 encodes proliferation marker protein Ki-67. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein that associates with the surface of mitotic chromosomes and acts both as a chromosome repellent during early mitosis and chromosome attractant during late mitosis. The MKI67 brush structure prevents chromosomes from collapsing into a single chromatin mass by forming a steric and electrostatic charge barrier: the protein has a high net electrical charge and acts as a surfactant, dispersing chromosomes and enabling independent chromosome motility. It binds DNA, with a preference for supercoiled DNA and AT-rich DNA. ([NCBI Gene 4288](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4288), [UniProt P46013](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P46013/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## MLH1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MLH1 encodes a component of DNA mismatch repair that partners with PMS2 to form MutL-alpha. Following mismatch recognition, this complex helps initiate removal of the incorrect DNA segment; PMS2 supplies the endonuclease activity that introduces a nearby single-strand break. MLH1 also participates in DNA-damage signaling and can pair with MLH3 in MutL-gamma, a separate complex with a role in meiosis. ([NCBI Gene 4292](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4292)). Germline disease associations include Lynch syndrome (autosomal dominant); Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Loss of mismatch-repair function involving MLH1 is relevant in colorectal and endometrial carcinomas. MLH1 promoter methylation is a distinct mechanism of tumor-associated silencing. ([AMP sporadic solid tumors — MMR deficiency](https://www.amp.org/AMP/assets/File/education/MIMP/SolidTumors_Sporadic.pdf)).

## MLLT1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MLLT1 encodes protein ENL. It is a chromatin reader component of the super elongation complex (SEC), a complex required to increase the catalytic rate of RNA polymerase II transcription by suppressing transient pausing by the polymerase at multiple sites along the DNA. It specifically recognizes and binds acetylated and crotonylated histones, with a preference for histones that are crotonylated. It has a slightly higher affinity for binding histone H3 crotonylated at 'Lys-27' (H3K27cr) than 'Lys-20' (H3K9cr20). ([NCBI Gene 4298](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4298), [UniProt Q03111](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q03111/entry)).

## MRE11

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MRE11 encodes double-strand break repair protein MRE11. Based in part on similarity, it is a core component of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage. ([NCBI Gene 4361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4361), [UniProt P49959](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P49959/entry)). Germline disease associations include ataxia-telangiectasia-like disorder 1 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic MRE11 alterations have been reported in ovarian carcinoma. ([PMID 24240112](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24240112/)).

## MRTFA

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MRTFA encodes myocardin-related transcription factor A. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription coactivator that associates with the serum response factor (SRF) transcription factor to control expression of genes regulating the cytoskeleton during development, morphogenesis and cell migration. ## MSH2

MSH2 encodes a DNA mismatch-recognition protein. It forms part of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR). ## MSH6

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MSH6 encodes a MutS-family mismatch-repair protein that forms a mismatch-recognition complex with MSH2. The complex binds and releases mismatched DNA through a nucleotide-dependent molecular switch involving exchange of ADP and ATP. Its role is therefore in recognition and regulated handling of a DNA mismatch, upstream of the steps that remove and replace the incorrect sequence. MTA1 encodes metastasis-associated protein MTA1. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a component of the histone deacetylase NuRD complex which participates in the remodeling of chromatin. It functions as a transcriptional coactivator of BCAS3, and SUMO2, independent of the NuRD complex. ([NCBI Gene 9112](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/9112), [UniProt Q13330](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q13330/entry)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation, somatic_association_requires_curation.

## MTAP

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MTAP encodes s-methyl-5'-thioadenosine phosphorylase. It catalyzes the phosphorolytic cleavage of S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine (MTA) to adenine and 5-methylthioribose1-phosphate. It participates in the breakdown of MTA, a major by-product of polyamine biosynthesis. It has broad substrate specificity with 6-aminopurine nucleosides as preferred substrates. ([NCBI Gene 4507](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4507), [UniProt Q13126](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q13126/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with diaphyseal medullary stenosis-bone malignancy syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic alterations involving MTAP have been reported in mesothelioma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## MTOR

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MTOR encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR. Based in part on similarity, it is a serine/threonine protein kinase which is a central regulator of cellular metabolism, growth and survival in response to hormones, growth factors, nutrients, energy and stress signals. MTOR directly or indirectly regulates the phosphorylation of at least 800 proteins. It acts as part of 2 structurally and functionally distinct signaling complexes mTORC1 and mTORC2 (mTOR complex 1 and 2). ([NCBI Gene 2475](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/2475), [UniProt P42345](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P42345/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with overgrowth syndrome and/or cerebral malformations due to abnormalities in MTOR pathway genes (autosomal dominant); macrocephaly-intellectual disability-neurodevelopmental disorder-small thorax syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 26542245](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26542245/)). Somatic alterations involving MTOR have been reported in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and endometrial carcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## MUC4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MUC4 encodes mucin-4. These glycoproteins play important roles in the protection of the epithelium and are implicated in epithelial renewal and differentiation. It regulates cellular behavior through both anti-adhesive effects on cell-cell and cell-extracellular matrix interactions and its ability to act as an intramembrane ligand for ERBB2. It contributes to proliferation and differentiation of epithelial cells by inducing specific phosphorylation of ERBB2. ([NCBI Gene 4585](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4585), [UniProt Q99102](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q99102/entry)).

## MUS81

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MUS81 encodes structure-specific endonuclease subunit MUS81. It is a catalytic subunit of two functionally distinct, structure-specific, heterodimeric DNA endonucleases MUS81-EME1 and MUS81-EME2 that are involved in the maintenance of genome stability. MUS81-EME1, on the other hand, is active later in the cell cycle and functions in the resolution of mitotic recombination intermediates including the Holliday junctions, the four-way DNA intermediates that form during homologous recombination. ([NCBI Gene 80198](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/80198), [UniProt Q96NY9](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q96NY9/entry)).

## MYBL1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MYBL1 encodes myb-related protein A. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a master regulator of male meiosis by promoting expression of piRNAs: activates expression of both piRNA precursor RNAs and expression of protein-coding genes involved in piRNA metabolism. ## MYD88

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MYD88 encodes an adaptor for Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor signaling that links receptor activation to downstream inflammatory signaling, including NF-κB activation. Based in part on similarity, it is an adapter protein involved in the Toll-like receptor and IL-1 receptor signaling pathway in the innate immune response. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

MYH9 encodes myosin-9. Based in part on similarity, it is required for cortical actin clearance prior to oocyte exocytosis. ## NBN

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

NBN encodes nibrin. It forms part of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage. ([NCBI Gene 4683](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/4683), [UniProt O60934](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O60934/entry)). Germline disease associations include Nijmegen breakage syndrome (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## NCOA1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

NCOA1 encodes nuclear receptor coactivator 1. It is a nuclear receptor coactivator that directly binds nuclear receptors and stimulates the transcriptional activities in a hormone-dependent fashion. It participates in the coactivation of different nuclear receptors, such as for steroids (PGR, GR and ER), retinoids (RXRs), thyroid hormone (TRs) and prostanoids (PPARs). It is also involved in coactivation mediated by STAT3, STAT5A, STAT5B and STAT6 transcription factors. ## NCOA4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

NCOA4 encodes nuclear receptor coactivator 4. It functions as an adapter for delivery of ferritin to lysosomes and autophagic degradation of ferritin, a process named ferritinophagy. ## NEIL3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA glycosylase which prefers single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), or partially ssDNA structures such as bubble and fork structures, to double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). ## NRAS

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

NRAS encodes a small GTPase whose activity is controlled by proteins that promote nucleotide exchange or stimulate GTP hydrolysis. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PAN3 encodes PAN2-PAN3 deadenylation complex subunit PAN3 (PAB1P-dependent poly(A)-specific ribonuclease) (Poly(A)-nuclease deadenylation complex subunit 3). ## PARP1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PARP1 encodes poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1. Based in part on similarity, it mediates glutamate, aspartate, serine, threonine, histidine or tyrosine ADP-ribosylation of proteins: the ADP-D-ribosyl group of NAD(+) is transferred to the acceptor carboxyl group of target residues and further ADP-ribosyl groups are transferred to the 2'-position of the terminal adenosine moiety, building up a polymer with an average chain length of 20-30 units. PHF6 encodes PHD finger protein 6. It participates in regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II and negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.
