## PHOX2B

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PHOX2B encodes paired mesoderm homeobox protein 2B. It participates in the development of several major noradrenergic neuron populations, including the locus coeruleus. It is a transcription factor which could determine a neurotransmitter phenotype in vertebrates. It enhances second-messenger-mediated activation of the dopamine beta-hydrolase and c-fos promoters, and of several enhancers including cAMP-response element and serum-response element. ([NCBI Gene 8929](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8929), [UniProt Q99453](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q99453/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Haddad syndrome (autosomal dominant); central hypoventilation syndrome, congenital, 1, with or without Hirschsprung disease (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## PICALM

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PICALM encodes phosphatidylinositol-binding clathrin assembly protein. It is a cytoplasmic adapter protein that plays a critical role in clathrin-mediated endocytosis which is important in processes such as internalization of cell receptors, synaptic transmission or removal of apoptotic cells. It recruits AP-2 and attaches clathrin triskelions to the cytoplasmic side of plasma membrane leading to clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs) assembly. Furthermore, regulates clathrin-coated vesicle size and maturation by directly sensing and driving membrane curvature. ([NCBI Gene 8301](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8301), [UniProt Q13492](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q13492/entry)). PICALM–MLLT10 rearrangements have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and lymphoid malignancies. ([NCBI Gene 8301](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8301)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## PIK3CA

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PIK3CA encodes the p110-alpha catalytic subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase. The enzyme combines a catalytic subunit with an approximately 85-kDa regulatory subunit and uses ATP to phosphorylate phosphoinositide lipids. Its normal role is therefore to generate lipid signaling products through regulated enzymatic activity. The distinction between catalytic and regulatory components is central to understanding its place in the PI3K signaling pathway. ([NCBI Gene 5290](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5290)). Germline disease associations include overgrowth syndrome and/or cerebral malformations due to abnormalities in MTOR pathway genes (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Postzygotic mosaic variants are associated with megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome. ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 22729224](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22729224/)). Somatic alterations involving PIK3CA have been reported in invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, endometrioid carcinoma of endometrium, and colorectal adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## PIK3CB

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PIK3CB encodes phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit beta isoform. It uses ATP and PtdIns(4,5)P2 (phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate) to generate phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3). PIP3 plays a key role by recruiting PH domain-containing proteins to the membrane, including AKT1 and PDPK1, activating signaling cascades involved in cell growth, survival, proliferation, motility and morphology. It participates in the activation of AKT1 upon stimulation by G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) ligands such as CXCL12, sphingosine 1-phosphate, and lysophosphatidic acid. ([NCBI Gene 5291](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5291), [UniProt P42338](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P42338/entry)). Somatic alterations involving PIK3CB have been reported in glioblastoma multiforme, prostate adenocarcinoma, and bladder urothelial carcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## PIM1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PIM1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase pim-1. ## PKHD1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PKHD1 encodes fibrocystin. Based in part on similarity, it promotes ciliogenesis in renal epithelial cells and therefore participates in the tubules formation and/ or ensures the maintenance of the architecture of the lumen of the kidney. It has an impact on cellular symmetry by ensuring correct bipolar cell division through the regulation of centrosome duplication and mitotic spindle assembly and by maintaining oriented cell division (OCD) during tubular elongation through planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway. It promotes cell-cell contact through the positive regulation of PTK2 kinase activity leading to either positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation through the HRAS/RAF1 pathways, or negative regulation of apoptosis through the PDK1/AKT1 pathway. ([NCBI Gene 5314](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5314), [UniProt P08F94](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P08F94/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (autosomal recessive); polycystic kidney disease 4 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## PMS2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PMS2 encodes the endonuclease component of MutL-alpha, a DNA mismatch-repair complex formed with MLH1. After MutS complexes recognize mismatches or insertion/deletion loops, MutL-alpha helps initiate removal of the incorrect DNA. PMS2 supplies the DNA-cutting activity, with a conserved carboxy-terminal motif contributing to its active site. This role distinguishes downstream incision of DNA from the initial recognition of the mismatch. ([NCBI Gene 5395](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5395)). Germline disease associations include Lynch syndrome (autosomal dominant); Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Loss of mismatch-repair function involving PMS2 is relevant in colorectal and endometrial carcinomas. ([AMP sporadic solid tumors — MMR deficiency](https://www.amp.org/AMP/assets/File/education/MIMP/SolidTumors_Sporadic.pdf)).

## PODXL

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PODXL encodes podocalyxin like. It acts as an anti-adhesive molecule that maintains an open filtration pathway between neighboring foot processes in the podocyte by charge repulsion. It functions as a pro-adhesive molecule, enhancing the adherence of cells to immobilized ligands, increasing the rate of migration and cell-cell contacts in an integrin-dependent manner. It induces the formation of apical actin-dependent microvilli. ([NCBI Gene 5420](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5420), [UniProt O00592](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O00592/entry)). Somatic alterations involving PODXL have been reported in adrenocortical carcinoma, papillary renal cell carcinoma, and clear cell renal cell carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## POLB

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

POLB encodes DNA polymerase beta. It conducts 'gap-filling' DNA synthesis in a stepwise distributive fashion rather than in a processive fashion as for other DNA polymerases. It is also able to cleave sugar-phosphate bonds 3' to an intact AP site, acting as an AP lyase. ([NCBI Gene 5423](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5423), [UniProt P06746](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P06746/entry)).

## POLD1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

POLD1 encodes the catalytic subunit of DNA polymerase delta, which participates in DNA replication and repair and provides proofreading exonuclease activity. It exhibits both DNA polymerase and 3'- to 5'-exonuclease activities. It requires the presence of accessory proteins POLD2, POLD3 and POLD4 for full activity. Pol-delta3 idling process may avoid the formation of a gap, while maintaining a nick that can be readily ligated. ([NCBI Gene 5424](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/5424), [UniProt P28340](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P28340/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with POLD1-related polyposis and colorectal cancer syndrome (autosomal dominant); mandibular hypoplasia-deafness-progeroid syndrome (autosomal dominant). Somatic alterations involving POLD1 have been reported in esophageal adenocarcinoma and invasive breast carcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## POLH

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

POLH encodes DNA polymerase eta. It is a DNA polymerase specifically involved in the DNA repair by translesion synthesis (TLS). ## POLQ

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

POLQ encodes DNA polymerase theta. Based in part on similarity, MMEJ is an error-prone repair pathway that produces deletions of sequences from the strand being repaired and promotes genomic rearrangements, such as telomere fusions, some of them leading to cellular transformation. MMEJ is required during mitosis to repair persistent double-strand breaks that originate in S-phase. ## POT1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

POT1 encodes protection of telomeres protein 1. It forms part of the telomerase ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex that is essential for the replication of chromosome termini. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PPP1R10 encodes serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 10. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

PRKCA encodes protein kinase C alpha type. This step is crucial for activation and normal distribution of EZR at the early stages of intestinal epithelial cell differentiation. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

## RAD50

RAD50 encodes DNA repair protein RAD50. ## RAD51C

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

RAD51C encodes a member of the RAD51 family involved in homologous recombination and DNA repair. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

RAD51D encodes a RAD51-family protein that participates in homologous recombination and DNA repair. It forms a complex with other RAD51 paralogs, including XRCC2. ## RNF8

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

RNF8 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RNF8. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

RTEL1 encodes regulator of telomere elongation helicase 1. It functions as an anti-recombinase to counteract toxic recombination and limit crossover during meiosis. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the signal recognition particle (SRP) complex, a ribonucleoprotein complex that mediates the cotranslational targeting of secretory and membrane proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The SRP complex interacts with the signal sequence in nascent secretory and membrane proteins and directs them to the membrane of the ER. The SRP complex targets the ribosome-nascent chain complex to the SRP receptor (SR), which is anchored in the ER, where SR compaction and GTPase rearrangement drive cotranslational protein translocation into the ER. ([NCBI Gene 6731](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/6731), [UniProt O76094](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O76094/entry)).

SRSF2 encodes a serine/arginine-rich RNA-binding splicing factor that regulates splice-site selection and processing of pre-mRNA. It is necessary for the splicing of pre-mRNA. STAG1 encodes cohesin subunit SA-1. It forms part of cohesin complex, a complex required for the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA replication. ## TDG

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TDG encodes G/T mismatch-specific thymine DNA glycosylase. It is a DNA glycosylase that plays a key role in active DNA demethylation: specifically recognizes and binds 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) in the context of CpG sites and mediates their excision through base-excision repair (BER) to install an unmethylated cytosine. It is also involved in DNA repair by acting as a thymine-DNA glycosylase that mediates correction of G/T mispairs to G/C pairs: in the DNA of higher eukaryotes, hydrolytic deamination of 5-methylcytosine to thymine leads to the formation of G/T mismatches. It is capable of hydrolyzing the carbon-nitrogen bond between the sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA and a mispaired thymine. ([NCBI Gene 6996](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/6996), [UniProt Q13569](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q13569/entry)).

## TERC

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TERC produces the RNA template component of telomerase. The telomerase ribonucleoprotein combines this template with a reverse-transcriptase protein component to add TTAGGG repeats at chromosome ends. TERC therefore supplies sequence information for telomere extension rather than the catalytic protein itself. Regulation of telomerase activity is linked to telomere maintenance and cellular senescence. ([NCBI Gene 7012](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7012)). Pathogenic constitutional TERC variants cause autosomal dominant dyskeratosis congenita, a telomere biology disorder associated with bone-marrow failure. ([PMID 11574891](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11574891/), [ClinGen SGC-107615.2](https://search.clinicalgenome.org/kb/gene-validity/CGGV:assertion_cfdf86d0-9441-40bf-a1da-ab2c85f775cd-2024-11-25T17:00:00.000Z)). Somatic copy-number gain involving the TERC region has been associated with progression of cervical neoplasia to invasive carcinoma. Regional gain is distinct from the constitutional loss-of-function mechanisms underlying telomere biology disorders. ([PMID 17054308](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17054308/)).

## TERT

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TERT encodes the catalytic reverse-transcriptase component of telomerase. Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme essential for the replication of chromosome termini in most eukaryotes. It is the catalytic component of the teleromerase holoenzyme complex whose main activity is the elongation of telomeres by acting as a reverse transcriptase that adds simple sequence repeats to chromosome ends by copying a template sequence within the RNA component of the enzyme. It catalyzes the RNA-dependent extension of 3'-chromosomal termini with the 6-nucleotide telomeric repeat unit, 5'-TTAGGG-3'. ([NCBI Gene 7015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7015), [UniProt O14746](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O14746/entry)). ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## TOP1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TOP1 encodes DNA topoisomerase 1. Based in part on similarity, it releases the supercoiling and torsional tension of DNA introduced during the DNA replication and transcription by transiently cleaving and rejoining one strand of the DNA duplex. ## TP53

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TP53 encodes p53, a tumor-suppressor transcription factor with DNA-binding, transcriptional-activation, and oligomerization domains. In response to cellular stress, p53 changes expression of target genes that control cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair, senescence, apoptosis, and metabolism. Alternative promoters, RNA splicing, and translation initiation produce multiple protein isoforms. These properties allow the gene to connect detection of cellular stress with several distinct growth-control and cell-fate responses. ([NCBI Gene 7157](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7157)). Germline pathogenic variants cause autosomal dominant Li-Fraumeni syndrome, which predisposes to a broad spectrum of cancers, notably early-onset breast cancer, sarcomas, central nervous system tumors, and adrenocortical carcinoma. ([GeneReviews: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1311/), [PMID 8118819](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8118819/), [PMID 1978757](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1978757/)). Somatic TP53 mutations occur across many cancer types. ([NCBI Gene 7157](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7157), [GeneReviews: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1311/)).

TSC1 encodes hamartin. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

VHL encodes a component of a ubiquitination complex that targets hypoxia-inducible factor for degradation. Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

XRCC5 encodes X-ray repair cross complementing 5. ## ZFHX3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZFHX3 encodes zinc finger homeobox protein 3. Based in part on similarity, it inhibits the enhancer element of the AFP gene by binding to its AT-rich core sequence. It regulates the circadian locomotor rhythms via transcriptional activation of neuropeptidergic genes which are essential for intercellular synchrony and rhythm amplitude in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the brain. ([NCBI Gene 463](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/463), [UniProt Q15911](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q15911/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ZFHX3 have been reported in vulva/Vagina, plasma cell myeloma, and endometrial carcinoma. ([IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ZFHX4

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZFHX4 encodes zinc finger homeobox protein 4. It participates in regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. Functional annotations also associate the protein with DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific. ([NCBI Gene 79776](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/79776), [UniProt Q86UP3](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q86UP3/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with syndromic complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)).

Curation note (outside report text): somatic_association_requires_curation.

## ZHX3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZHX3 encodes zinc fingers and homeoboxes 3. Its functions include DNA-binding transcription factor activity and DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific. ([NCBI Gene 23051](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/23051), [UniProt Q9H4I2](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9H4I2/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ZHX3 have been reported in colorectal carcinoma, gastric adenocarcinoma, and bladder urothelial carcinoma. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

## ZMYM2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZMYM2 encodes zinc finger MYM-type protein 2. It participates in negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription. Functional annotations also associate the protein with ubiquitin conjugating enzyme binding. ([NCBI Gene 7750](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7750), [UniProt Q9UBW7](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9UBW7/entry)). Pathogenic germline variants are associated with syndromic complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); neurodevelopmental-craniofacial syndrome with variable renal and cardiac abnormalities (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download), [PMID 37383123](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37383123/)). Somatic alterations involving ZMYM2 have been reported in myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with tyrosine kinase fusion and prostate adenocarcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

## ZNRF3

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZNRF3 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase ZNRF3. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of Wnt receptor complex components Frizzled and LRP6. It acts on both canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway. ([NCBI Gene 84133](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/84133), [UniProt Q9ULT6](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9ULT6/entry)). Somatic alterations involving ZNRF3 have been reported in adrenocortical carcinoma. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/), [IntOGen 20240920](https://www.intogen.org/download?file=IntOGen-Drivers-20240920.zip)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.

## ZRSR2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ZRSR2 encodes a splicing factor important for recognition and processing of introns, particularly those handled by the minor spliceosome. It selectively interacts with the 3'-splice site of U2- and U12-type pre-mRNAs and promotes different steps in U2 and U12 intron splicing. ([NCBI Gene 8233](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8233), [UniProt Q15696](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q15696/entry)). Somatic ZRSR2 mutations occur in myelodysplastic neoplasms. ([PMID 22389253](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22389253/)).

Curation note (outside report text): germline_association_requires_curation.
